key_insight: ColorConceptBench provides the first human-annotated, probabilistic benchmark for how text-to-image models map implicit color concepts to color distributions, enabling evaluation beyond single color names or codes.
problem_solved: Existing evaluations focus on explicit color labels and ignore the inherent ambiguity of implicit color concepts; this benchmark quantifies color–concept associations as probability distributions derived from human judgments so models can be assessed more realistically.
method: Curate 1,281 implicit color concepts and collect 6,369 human annotations to build ground-truth probabilistic color distributions.
Generate images or color predictions from T2I models for each concept and extract color distributions (e.g., color histograms / palette probabilities).
Compare model-derived distributions to human distributions using distributional similarity metrics to measure alignment with human color expectations.
impact: Provides practitioners a practical tool for diagnosing color understanding and generation in T2I systems, guiding model/data improvements for more human-aligned and nuanced color rendering.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: prompt (implicit concept) → model generation → color extraction → distribution comparison with human annotations.
Side-by-side bar charts or probability histograms showing human vs. model color distributions for representative concepts (e.g., 'autumn leaf', 'ocean mood').
Concept×Color heatmap summarizing probabilistic associations across many concepts (shows where models deviate at scale).
Dataset summary card: iconography for 1,281 concepts and 6,369 human annotations to convey scale and human grounding.
paper_title: ColorConceptBench: A Benchmark for Probabilistic Color-Concept Understanding in Text-to-Image Models
paper_authors: Chenxi Ruan, Yu Xiao, Yihan Hou, Guosheng Hu, Wei Zeng
